diagnostic_evidence.quote: where $\es_i:=\es_{\mathbf{1}_i}$ denotes the forward shift with respect to $n^i$

issues.failure_explanation: The operator d_h^Δ is built from forward differences S_i − id along the coordinate axes. For p=1, the element −1 of GL(1,Z) turns forward shifts into backward shifts. In the new coordinate, Δ^m(f(n−1)−f(n)) cannot equal Δ^n(f(n+1)−f(n)) for all f under any translation-invariant relation Δ^m=cΔ^n. A shear in GL(2,Z) fails the same way: the new forward shift is S_1^{-1}S_2. The remark therefore claims an invariance that the definitions do not have.

failure_location.quote: namely $GL(p,\mathbb{Z})$ transformations of the base space $\mathbb{Z}^p$

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict the invariance claim to translations (and permutations of the lattice directions), or describe how d_h^Δ transforms under general lattice maps.
issues.overall_effect: The asserted coordinate-independence of the horizontal operator is overstated. Only translations and permutations of axes are supported.
issues.title: False claim that the exterior difference is invariant under all GL(p,Z) changes of base coordinates
issues.why_classification: This is a side remark that later arguments do not use. Correcting the stated symmetry group is a local fix that leaves every result intact.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: This implies the existence (locally) of a $(p,0)$-form
(However, these equations may be weaker than the given system and so admit other solutions.)

issues.failure_explanation: The paper obtains L only from the identity d_h^Δη = d_v L restricted to the solution set. It then applies I^Δ, which involves partial derivatives with respect to all prolongation coordinates and backward shifts, to that on-shell identity. This operation does not commute with restriction, and no off-shell Lagrangian on the full prolongation space is constructed. Even granting the step, the argument shows at most that solutions of the system satisfy the Euler–Lagrange equations, not that those equations are the system. The paper itself makes this caveat in the differential case.

issues.title: On-shell construction does not show L is a Lagrangian for the given PΔE system

diagnostic_evidence.quote: As $\mcI^{\vartriangle}$ is a projection and the difference variational bicomplex is exact, a difference version of equality \eqref{eq:ii} holds.

issues.failure_explanation: Equation (eq:ii) is the differential identity. Its difference analogue was obtained in Section 3 only by assuming exactness of the difference bicomplex, which is what this theorem is meant to prove. The homotopy identity (eq:hohomo) involves h^{k+1,l}, which is undefined for k=p, so it covers only k≤p−1. For k=p it would wrongly make every (p,l)-form exact. Exactness at Ω^{p,l} (ker I^Δ = im d_h^Δ) is therefore assumed rather than proved. Theorem thm:added-4 uses the same difference version of (eq:ii) for σ = I^Δσ + d_h^Δτ.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Prove directly a top-degree homotopy formula σ = I^Δ(σ) + d_h^Δ h^{p,l}(σ) for σ∈Ω^{p,l}, e.g. by summation by parts, and use it in place of the citation of (eq:ii) in both appendix proofs.
issues.overall_effect: Exactness of the augmented horizontal rows at Ω^{p,l} and the edge-complex argument are unproven. So is the difference version of (eq:ii) used for the Noether law and the Section 5 constructions.
issues.title: Circular justification of ker I^Δ = im d_h^Δ in the exactness proof
issues.why_classification: The result is standard and recoverable with a contained homotopy argument, without new global architecture. As written, though, the central exactness claim lacks a non-circular proof.
